title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Romans 9: the writer's sorrow for his relatives, the children of the promise, the potter and the clay, and the stumbling stone.

questions.text: What does the writer say he has in his heart for his relatives according to the flesh?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:2-3 say he has great sorrow and unceasing pain in his heart, and could wish himself accursed from Christ for his brothers' sake.

questions.text: Which of these is listed in the text as belonging to the Israelites?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:4 lists the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises as theirs.

questions.text: Through whom will Abraham's offspring be accounted, according to the quotation?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:7 quotes, “your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac.”

questions.text: What is the word of promise quoted about Sarah?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:9 quotes the word of promise, “At the appointed time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”

answers.text: “Sarah will laugh when she hears my promise.”
“At the appointed time Sarah will be the mother of kings.”
“Sarah will see her offspring as the stars of heaven.”
“At the appointed time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”

questions.text: What was said to Rebekah before her children were born?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:10-12 say that Rebekah conceived by Isaac, and that before the children were born and had done anything good or bad, it was said to her, “The elder will serve the younger.”

questions.text: What did God say to Moses, according to the text?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:15 says he told Moses, “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”

answers.text: “I will show mercy to all who ask.”
“I will have mercy on whom I have mercy.”
“I will judge every man by his works.”

questions.text: For what purpose does the Scripture say Pharaoh was raised up?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:17 says the Scripture tells Pharaoh he was caused to be raised up so that God's power might be shown in him and his name proclaimed in all the earth.

answers.text: So that Israel might serve him and his house forever
So that the riches of Egypt might be made known to all
So that God's power might be shown and his name proclaimed in all the earth
So that the law might be given to him and to his servants

questions.text: Who, in the text's image, has a right over the clay?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:21 asks whether the potter does not have a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel for honor and another for dishonor.

questions.text: In which prophet does the writer find the words “I will call them ‘my people,’ which were not my people”?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:25 says that he says this also in Hosea.

questions.text: What did Israel stumble over, according to the end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:32 says they did not seek righteousness by faith but as it were by works of the law, and they stumbled over the stumbling stone.
